No—the clean version is a modest layout change, not a significant complication.

The current hierarchy is:

```text
Full-width project header
Left pane | Canvas | Divider | Agent pane
```

The requested hierarchy would be:

```text
Left pane | Project header + Canvas | Divider | Agent pane
```

The implementation is localized to [ShellController.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:420):

- Add the existing `StatusRow` to `m_workspace_sizer`, above the canvas.
- Remove its full-width insertion into `main_sizer`.
- Adjust the corresponding detach logic during shell uninstall.
- Update the layout harness to assert that the header and canvas have the same horizontal bounds.

The left pane already paints its divider for its entire height in [LeftPane.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/LeftPane.cpp:765), and the Agent divider also paints its full height in [ShellController.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:91). Once the header is nested in the center column, both red lines naturally extend to the top.

The only meaningful complication is narrow-window behavior. `StatusRow` currently assumes the full window width when arranging Home, the printer/filament chip, Slice, panel toggle, and overflow in [StatusRow.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:270). The test harness shrinks the window as far as 760 DIP, leaving the center column quite narrow. We would need to verify—and possibly improve—how the chip collapses so the buttons never overlap.

My assessment:

- Basic geometry: low complexity, probably under 20 substantive layout lines.
- Production-ready change with resize and cross-platform verification: low-to-medium complexity.
- No changes to slicing, canvas, Agent state, or pane behavior should be necessary.

I recommend moving the whole project header into the middle column. If “Slice must be the literal last control at the separator” means the panel-toggle and overflow controls should remain over the Agent pane, that would require splitting the current `StatusRow` and would be noticeably more involved.
